title: Bad News
novel: Marshall and Lily had been trying to have a baby for months without success. They were growing [[increasingly|increasingly]] worried and decided to visit a [[fertility|fertility]] specialist. The doctor ran a series of tests on both of them. While they waited for the results, Marshall tried to stay [[optimistic|optimistic]], but Lily could see the [[fear|fear]] in his eyes. They feared they would never get pregnant. Meanwhile, Robin started her new job at a morning talk show. She had to work with an [[annoying|annoy]] co-host who constantly interrupted her and made [[childish|childish]] jokes. Robin found it difficult to stay [[professional|professional]] when her partner was so [[immature|immature]]. Barney tried to [[distract|distract]] Marshall from his worries by taking him to a botany class, but Marshall could not focus. He kept checking his phone for the doctor's call. Throughout the episode, a hidden [[countdown|countdown]] ticked from 50 down to 1. Numbers appeared in the background of nearly every scene: on [[license|license]] plates, menus, clocks, and signs. The gang did not notice the countdown at all. When the doctor finally called, Marshall learned that he was perfectly [[healthy|healthy]] and fertile. Lily was also fine. There was no medical reason they could not [[conceive|conceive]]. They were [[relieved|relief]] beyond words. However, just as Marshall arrived home to share the good news with his father over the phone, the countdown reached zero. Lily answered Marshall's phone and received a different call. Marvin Eriksen Sr., Marshall's father, had suffered a sudden [[heart|heart]] attack and passed away. The news hit Marshall like a [[freight|freight]] train. He collapsed into Lily's arms, [[sobbing|sob]] uncontrollably. The gang stood in stunned [[silence|silence]], realizing that life could change in an instant.

increasingly.en: more and more as time goes on

optimistic.en: hoping for the best in a situation

fear.en: an unpleasant feeling of danger or worry

annoy.en: to make someone feel slightly angry

childish.en: behaving like a child, not mature

professional.en: showing proper skill and behavior at work

immature.en: not behaving like an adult should

countdown.en: the act of counting backward to zero

conceive.en: to become pregnant with a child

relief.en: feeling better after worry goes away

heart.en: the organ that pumps blood in the body

freight.en: goods transported by truck or train

sob.en: to cry noisily while breathing in gasps

silence.en: a complete lack of sound or speech
